transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, I came in because I just... I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. It happens a lot in the radiology suite, or when I'm in class. I've been trying to just tough it out for months now, but it's not working. I always end up pacing, or shifting around constantly, or just finding some excuse so I can get up and move.
Did this feeling start after you began a new medication or changed the dose of one?
No, I haven't started any new medications. I actually don't take anything right now, so... yeah, it's definitely not from a medication or a dose change.
Did you have this same hard-to-sit-still feeling when you were a child?

Yeah, I did. My parents actually still talk about my elementary school conferences. The teachers would always tell them I was constantly out of my seat, calling out, or just rushing ahead before they even finished giving directions. So it's been going on for a long time. It was happening way before middle school, definitely not just since I started my radiology training.
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about many different things?

No, I don't think so. I don't really spend much time worrying about things. It's not like my mind is stuck on anxious thoughts or anything like that, it's just... I just physically feel like I need to keep moving. So no, worrying isn't really an issue for me.
